A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CraftRTL work. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, and figures. Earlier Appendices B-D correspond to later Appendices C-E; moved and redrawn figures can also be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original VerilogEval and RTLLM evaluations, training-data and quality-control ablations, scaling experiments, and code-diversity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds error-type frequencies, selected problems' checkpoint trajectories, and a direct-prompting repair result.

M1.justification: The correct-by-construction generators, targeted error-report and repair pipeline, model architectures, and training objective are retained. The detailed prompt templates are unchanged after appendix renumbering. Expanded sampling explanations and the redrawn pipeline document the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training sources, VerilogEval-Machine/Human, the 45-problem NonText subset, RTLLM v1.1, and generated in-distribution non-textual tests. New analyses examine existing errors and benchmark problems. Other languages and visual representations are discussed without additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Section 3.2 newly reports direct LLM prompting without detailed error reports as a repair comparator, resolving 13% of errors. This differs from the retained Table 7 ablation of error reports during repair-data generation. The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds the direct-prompting repair control and Pearson correlation as a quantitative checkpoint-agreement measure. The existing benchmark protocol retains 20 samples per problem, temperatures 0.2 and 0.8, and one-epoch training. Appendix A.10 discloses checkpoint choices rather than establishing a change to those experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.9 analyzes error-type frequencies, and A.10 adds trajectories for five volatile benchmark problems. Section 3.2 adds the direct-prompting repair check. These supplement the retained training-data, quality-control, scaling, iterative-repair, and code-diversity analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 1 newly reports Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.638 for SDG and 0.782 for SDG-CC-Repair; v1's corresponding scatterplots lacked these statistical summaries. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-training seed statistics.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores, including Tables 4-14, are retained. New results include the 13% direct-prompting repair rate, error frequencies such as 15.3% vector-concatenation errors in Table 15, checkpoint trajectories in Table 17, and the correlation coefficients in Figure 1.

T1.justification: The pass@k definition, Boolean-construction reasoning, and FSM construction are unchanged. The expanded discussion introduces no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about correct-by-construction data and targeted repair. The stated benchmark improvements of 3.8%, 10.9%, and 6.6% are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands applicability and limitations: transfer may require human tuning, repair is argued to extend to other low-resource languages, and representation coverage is constrained by available benchmarks. It also discusses other hardware languages and prospective visual applications. Appendix A.9 adds hardware-specific interpretations of the error categories.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproducibility statement identifying access to the data-generation pipeline, exact checkpoint steps and epochs in Table 16, and details about sampling error reports and code snippets. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, evaluation processing, and prompt templates are retained. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of changed implementation.

R1.justification: Appendix B substantially expands positioning against automatic program repair, mined bug-fix datasets, code preference learning, and low-resource language transfer. Nine added references include Defects4J, Tufano et al., Xia et al., CodeDPO, and hardware DSL and multimodal evaluations. Appendix A.10 also adds an explicit priority claim concerning the observed volatility and its mitigation.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged. v2 adds Appendices A.9-A.10, a discussion appendix, and a reproducibility statement, with local wording corrections, updated cross-references, and a conference-publication header. The original example and prompt appendices are renumbered.

P2.justification: Key displays are substantially reorganized: v1 Figures 1 and 5 become the paired Figure 1; Figure 2 is split and moved to appendix Figures 26-28; the repair pipeline and scaling plot are redrawn. v2 also adds Tables 15-17, annotates Table 6 with data quantities, and revises highlighting in Tables 4 and 5.

improvement.justification: The added error analysis, checkpoint trajectories and disclosures, code-access information, and applicability qualifications make the existing work easier to assess and reproduce. Reorganized figures improve comparison. The gains remain limited: the core empirical evidence is unchanged, the new 13% repair control is sparsely specified, and broader transfer claims remain untested.
